notes.title: Le Mans Ultimate September V1.1 Update
notes.content: [h1]Le Mans Ultimate adds first ELMS content & Custom Livery improvements [/h1][p align="start"]  [/p][p align="start"]Following a landmark summer that saw the game achieve record daily and concurrent player numbers with its Version 1.0 launch, the latest update delivers significant new content with the addition of European Le Mans Series and features that expand both the scope and accessibility of the title. Here’s everything you need to know about our next release on 23rd September…[/p][p][/p][h3]European Le Mans Series joins the grid![/h3][p align="start"]We announced it alongside the ACO in June but we are already here with it’s first installment.[/p][p align="start"]In this release we are unlocking the ELMS race weekend format for all players on the tracks that are released and available so far. All players will also be receiving (for FREE) access to ELMS liveries and the unrestricted LMP2 car that races in ELMS - which has also been revisited on the physics side. Additionally, so you can see the difference when on track and in the menus, we’ve added a new LMP2 icon for the faster specification to the UI to make things a bit clearer which specification of car is racing.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44213141/4dd8050f85e90de1a17a5e6f0450cfe392066200.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"]ELMS DLC will have 3 packs - each with 1 car and 1 track. This will also be available in a Season Pass format for a discount which will automatically unlock as we release the packs. Pack 1 will be available on 23rd September, alongside this update, Pack 2 is expected before the end of the year and Pack 3 will be in the first quarter of 2026.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]The price will be [b]£8.99 / €9.99 / $11.99[/b] per pack but it will also be available in Season Pass at [b]£21.99 / €24.99 / $28.99[/b] with a further 10% launch discount for a limited time only.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]So what’s in Pack 1? We are delighted to welcome Silverstone - ELMS is visiting the iconic British circuit for the first time since 2019 and will prove an incredible circuit for these cars and this series. As always, this is an officially licensed and laser scanned track, created with utmost love, care and attention. You should expect no less from a simulation.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]As ELMS races from the classic “National” pitlane, this is the variation you’ll find upon release but we’re happy to confirm that we will be adding the Grand Prix pitlane option as well as the National and International shorter layouts in a future update. Additionally, the tracks in the game that ELMS already races at will receive a boost to 44 car grids in a later release.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]The first of three LMP3 cars coming in the ELMS pack is the Ligier JS P325 - the latest and most modern of this class out available for racing in this category. Featuring a 3.5L Toyota V6 Bi Turbo outputting 470 bhp this car is a wonderful example of modern prototype engineering and will no-doubt create some memorable on track experiences. We really hope you enjoy this new class and series in Le Mans Ultimate.[/p][p][/p][h3]Custom Livery Improvements & LiveryHub[/h3][p align="start"]We have been delighted to see the response to the custom livery feature we added in June with over [b]93,000[/b] uploaded so far but it’s time to up the ante. In this release we are bring a number of great new additions.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Firstly, it is now possible to drive and view your livery in a single player Race Weekend session. No longer do you need to load into an online lobby to take pretty pictures of your wonderful creation or race it against other icons in a recreated 2025 24 Hours of Le Mans for example.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Additionally, we’re pleased that custom numbers are now working and that you can use liveries on every server - including practice servers and hosted servers without entry lists - making league hosting more flexible than before.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Finally, thanks to our partners at SimGrid we’re presenting to you for the first time the ability to share and add liveries to your team via the [b]“LiveryHub”[/b]. Here creators can set their liveries to “public” and then add some tags for visibility. You can then search and find liveries you like to you your team which will then be automatically available in game.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44213141/216dfad8fdefd5b9d209570ba11c4e7ad635927e.png"][/img][/p][p align="start"]For those of you new to the custom liveries feature, you do need to be a RaceControl Pro or Pro+ subscriber which pays for the maintenance of the infrastructure we use to create the UI imagery on-the-fly and transfer the liveries automatically to all players. We also need to moderate the service as part of our license commitments.[/p][p][/p][h3]Regional Hosted Servers[/h3][p align="start"]Good news league racers - we’re adding server locations! So far all servers have been located in our European server farms which, in some cases despite our industry leading netcode, causes some issues particularly when multiple racers are far away from the server which can cause some latency due to the unfortunate laws of physics.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Therefore, we are adding new options for servers in [b]Asia[/b] and [b]North America[/b], alongside the existing [b]European[/b] default location. You can now select this when setting up your server on [url="http://racecontrol.gg/"][u]racecontrol.gg[/u][/url] or on SimGrid. The investment you make in us, means we’re able to push this back into scaling our service.[/p][p][/p][h3]Additional Improvements[/h3][p align="start"]Car select has been tidied up once again - we realised that the year filter was getting in the way of finding your favourites. We have also added in icons to easily see cars that are in your virtual garage so you don’t mindlessly click around when you first download the game to see what content you own.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Fans of TrackIR can now rejoice - it has been added to the sim natively. We hope you’ll make the most of it to check your blindspots…[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]We are also very pleased to be adding Simplified Chinese language option as well. Huge thanks to Xudong - one of our community members who spearheaded this project and passed it over to our team to implement. We hope the growing LMU Chinese community will be excited to access the game in their native language. We are just getting started with the ramping up of localised languages so watch this space.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]We will also be making some changes to the sizes of the Driver Rank brackets. Silver has been smaller than the other brackets, which has made changes in rating from race to race seem much bigger than they actually are. The effect of this is it is likely when we deploy this update that drivers ranked Silver 2 or above will move down compared to where they are currently.[/p][p align="start"]Of course, as always that isn’t everything - make sure you read the full release notes when they get posted.[/p][p][/p][h3]What’s next for LMU?[/h3][p align="start"]We’re working hard at a number of things here, as always. You now know of course that more ELMS content will come pack-by-pack and we expect the next car and track to release before the end of the year.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]We are still working on the “career mode” but nothing that we can share at this time.[/p][p align="start"]For the next release, we’ve got a number of online rules related features to help stamp out the worst offenders - in the meantime keep reporting players for deliberate collisions in Daily Races and for racing incidents only in Online Championships. We are adding more resources here as we know you value LMU as one of the premier online sim racing titles.[/p][p align="start"]We are also aware that you’re waiting to host your own team endurance races, we are targeting hosted team endurance races in the next release as well.[/p][p][/p][h3]Message from the studio[/h3][p align="start"][b]Stephen Hood, CEO of Motorsport Games & Head of Studio 397[/b] said - “We are extremely excited to be adding another endurance series with the European Le Mans Series with even more tracks and a new class of racing. We're excited to see if players enjoy this as much as we have during its development.”[/p]

tags.feature: In this release we are unlocking the ELMS race weekend format for all players on the tracks that are released and available so far. All players will also be receiving (for FREE) access to ELMS liveries and the unrestricted LMP2 car that races in ELMS - which has also been revisited on the physics side. Additionally, so you can see the difference when on track and in the menus, we’ve added a new LMP2 icon for the faster specification to the UI to make things a bit clearer which specification of car is racing.

ELMS DLC will have 3 packs - each with 1 car and 1 track. This will also be available in a Season Pass format for a discount which will automatically unlock as we release the packs. Pack 1 will be available on 23rd September, alongside this update, Pack 2 is expected before the end of the year and Pack 3 will be in the first quarter of 2026.

As ELMS races from the classic “National” pitlane, this is the variation you’ll find upon release but we’re happy to confirm that we will be adding the Grand Prix pitlane option as well as the National and International shorter layouts in a future update. Additionally, the tracks in the game that ELMS already races at will receive a boost to 44 car grids in a later release.

The first of three LMP3 cars coming in the ELMS pack is the Ligier JS P325 - the latest and most modern of this class out available for racing in this category. Featuring a 3.5L Toyota V6 Bi Turbo outputting 470 bhp this car is a wonderful example of modern prototype engineering and will no-doubt create some memorable on track experiences. We really hope you enjoy this new class and series in Le Mans Ultimate.

Firstly, it is now possible to drive and view your livery in a single player Race Weekend session. No longer do you need to load into an online lobby to take pretty pictures of your wonderful creation or race it against other icons in a recreated 2025 24 Hours of Le Mans for example.

Additionally, we’re pleased that custom numbers are now working and that you can use liveries on every server - including practice servers and hosted servers without entry lists - making league hosting more flexible than before.

Finally, thanks to our partners at SimGrid we’re presenting to you for the first time the ability to share and add liveries to your team via the “LiveryHub”. Here creators can set their liveries to “public” and then add some tags for visibility. You can then search and find liveries you like to you your team which will then be automatically available in game.

Therefore, we are adding new options for servers in Asia and North America, alongside the existing European default location. You can now select this when setting up your server on racecontrol.gg or on SimGrid. The investment you make in us, means we’re able to push this back into scaling our service.

Car select has been tidied up once again - we realised that the year filter was getting in the way of finding your favourites. We have also added in icons to easily see cars that are in your virtual garage so you don’t mindlessly click around when you first download the game to see what content you own.
Fans of TrackIR can now rejoice - it has been added to the sim natively. We hope you’ll make the most of it to check your blindspots…

We are also very pleased to be adding Simplified Chinese language option as well. Huge thanks to Xudong - one of our community members who spearheaded this project and passed it over to our team to implement. We hope the growing LMU Chinese community will be excited to access the game in their native language. We are just getting started with the ramping up of localised languages so watch this space.

tags.balance_change: We will also be making some changes to the sizes of the Driver Rank brackets. Silver has been smaller than the other brackets, which has made changes in rating from race to race seem much bigger than they actually are. The effect of this is it is likely when we deploy this update that drivers ranked Silver 2 or above will move down compared to where they are currently.

tags.feature: We are adding more resources here as we know you value LMU as one of the premier online sim racing titles.
We are also aware that you’re waiting to host your own team endurance races, we are targeting hosted team endurance races in the next release as well.

notes.title: Le Mans Ultimate V1.0 Update
notes.content:
[h3]Community Thanks
[/h3][p]From everyone at Motorsport Games & Studio 397 - thank you to all of you that have supported our project through Early Access. It has not been an easy journey for the game or our company but we’re pleased to have made it here thanks to everyone’s support - both in purchasing the game but also those of you that have helped through reports to refine any issues we had with releases.[/p][p]In particular, we want to address the last release - a lot of technical code changes were made in order to accommodate driver swaps and custom liveries. This caused some issues for some players. Thanks to your clear and concise feedback, we have tracked down these issues and have delivered three major patches between this release and in the last one (patch 3), in particular we have fixed networking issues for players with specific Internet Service Provider network types (CGNAT) having unexpected player consequences that really could never have been found without your help.[/p][p]These are the types of scenarios that Early Access was built for - we just don’t have the internal testing capacity to check every piece of hardware or 100s of different ISP network configurations. The good news is - we’re now done with those major changes, but it was vital to do this before the release of “version 1.0”.
[/p][h3]What’s new in v1.0?
[/h3][p]This is the grown-up, more mature June release but with some special new toys.[/p][p]The Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR LMH and Mercedes AMG LMGT3 are coming to the base game [b]FREE[/b] of charge. The incredible noise of that V12 engine in the Valkyrie will impress you both onboard behind the wheel, and from the trackside view.

The Mercedes, with its slick look is a fan favourite in GT3 racing across the globe and has been lovingly recreated in Le Mans Ultimate in never-before-seen detail.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44213141/3ccc44c95843f473d3a5a0cba144de1f0ad5b123.jpg"][/img]We didn’t mention it before but, we found some time to squeeze in the BMW M4 Evo LMGT3 as used by Team WRT this year. Included to all owners of this DLC content (available in 2024 Pack 3), we’ve updated this model for the 2025 season, with its brand new head and tail lights, wing mirrors and hood vents - it’s a stunner![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44213141/6f1cda05a86237a4d8bbcde0868053f79015f65c.jpg"][/img]
On the subject of LMGT3 - we heard your feedback on the new tyre model in the June release. Although we feel like it was a step in the right direction in reducing over-reliance on slip angle for speed, we appreciate the cliff-edge of grip felt a bit steep. We already made some improvements via patches to the setups which were not in the correct operating window. However, for this release we have also made some changes to the thermals of the tyres to increase the performance range as well as smoothing off the drop in performance amongst other things that are being continually improved - we think they’ll be a very positive improvement for all levels of driver.

We have also bought the simulation up to 2025 spec. There are new position boards on the cars where appropriate and added liveries to make the grid an even more colourful place than before. LMP2 Le Mans 2025 liveries will be coming soon.
[/p][p]Content isn’t the only place we’ve made improvements. We’ve made a few user experience changes as well. Firstly - the Race Weekend season select needed some work to add the 2025 calendar, and secondly - we’ve refined the car setup page! No longer do you need to go to several menus to change the really important things like virtual energy, tyres and electronics. It’s all here - condensed and ready to get you back out on track quicker than before. [/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44213141/6b6ba75de16d6430a7d91199acf55602eaa18f49.png"][/img][/p][p]And finally, we’re repackaging some things on the steam store. The “free DLCs” - BMW M Hybrid LMDh, McLaren 720S and Ford Mustang LMGT3 are both in the base game now to make things a little clearer. We’ve also created a new bundle - the Le Mans Ultimate WEC Full Access bundle - which is setup to be an easy step in to all the content we’ve fully delivered so far. And - if you don’t have all the 2024 packs you’ll be given a discount to “complete the set”.[/p][p][/p][p]Version 1.0 will be available on Steam at a 13% launch discount from the SRP (£28.99 / €34.99 / $37.99) until 5th August (after Racing Fest sale on Steam). After this point, the game's SRP will increase to £34.99 / €39.99 / $39.99. The WEC Full Access Bundle will be available at a 15% discount.[/p][h3]
Things to look forward to
[/h3][p]As we announced in June, the development team is still hard at work on Le Mans Ultimate, well beyond the upcoming version 1.0 release.
[/p][p]We are working on delivering the European Le Mans Series content and I’m pleased to share some early previews of buildings in Silverstone as we accelerate development of this project. We will be on-site at Silverstone during the ELMS weekend between the 12th and 14th September with a special build just for those of you there.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44213141/1390c14d244ad692ece2171e93ba792fe2e03c56.png"][/img] [/p][p]As we’ve already mentioned, work on career mode is underway with us expecting to deliver a unique single player experience in early 2026.
[/p][p]That’s not the only feature we’re working on - keep voting on our forum pages for what you want most even when we’ve left early access. We’re keeping an eye on it!
[/p][h3]Message from the studio
[/h3][p][b]Stephen Hood, CEO of Motorsport Games and Head of Studio 397[/b] said - “Thank you again to all the players and supports of Le Mans Ultimate since we launched in Early Access, for whom without we would have not reached this V1.0 Milestone. Keep pushing on track, enjoy the new content and I’ll see you again very soon.”[/p]

notes.title: June 2025 - Update #5 - release notes
notes.content: [h1]Update 5 with Driver Swaps, Team Management, Custom Liveries & Final 2024 content arrive in our biggest update yet[/h1][p][/p][p]Our update is here, and it’s arguably the most feature-packed release [i]Le Mans Ultimate[/i] has seen since launching into Early Access.[/p][p]From delivering driver swaps to building out full team functionality and unleashing a brand-new custom livery system, this update takes endurance racing in [i]Le Mans Ultimate[/i] to the next level. Oh, and we’re also rounding out the 2024 FIA WEC grid with new cars and circuits. Let’s get into it.[/p][quote][p]📄 [b]Read the full list of changes in the [url="https://lemansultimate.com/update-5-june-2025-release-notes/"]Release Notes[/url].[/b][/p][p]❗ [b]Check out current [url="https://lemansultimate.com/known-issues/"]Known Issues[/url].[/b][/p][/quote][h3][b]Driver Swaps: True Endurance Racing Arrives[/b][/h3][p]We’ve been working hard behind the scenes to bring you a much-requested feature - live driver swaps. You can now share your car with a teammate during online endurance events and hand over control mid-race just like in real-world WEC.[/p][p]Whether you’re managing pitstops, driving your stint, or cheering your teammate on, it’s a whole new level of teamwork and strategy. [u]For now, driver swaps are available in special curated events[/u] while we monitor performance of this new feature and polish the experience further.[/p][quote][p]👉 [i]Want to know when driver swap events are happening? Follow our website, social channels and check in-game announcements regularly.[/i][/p][/quote][hr][/hr][h3][b]Introducing Teams: Create, Manage & Race Together[/b][/h3][p]We’ve launched a team management system powered by RaceControl. Build your squad, assign roles (Driver, Engineer, Manager, Team Owner), and register for events together. It’s built directly into the game - no spreadsheets or external tools required.[/p][p]You’ll also see new DR/SR values attached to each lineup, meaning your team’s progress reflects your performance.[/p][quote][p][i]📘 Learn how to set up your own team with our [url="https://lemansultimate.com/teams/"]Team Creation and Management Guide[/url].[/i][/p][/quote][hr][/hr][h3][b]Custom Liveries Are Here[/b][/h3][p]You asked, and we’ve delivered: custom liveries have landed in [i]Le Mans Ultimate[/i]. Now you can design your car’s paint scheme and share it with all drivers and spectators during online events.[/p][p]All players can use the showroom to try out the custom livery but only RaceControl Pro and Pro+ players can use our livery upload tool. When you choose a custom livery car, your beautiful machine will be automatically viewable by everyone in a session.[/p][p]Support for private servers is coming in a future update.[/p][quote][p][i]🎨 Get started with the [url="https://lemansultimate.com/creating-custom-liveries/"]Custom Livery Guide[/url].[/i][/p][/quote][hr][/hr][h3][b]Final 2024 Content Pack: Complete the Grid[/b][/h3][p]This update also sees the arrival of [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3511300/Le_Mans_Ultimate__2024_Pack_5/"]Pack 5[/url] - the final drop for the 2024 WEC season. Say hello to:[/p][list][*][p][b]Lusail International Circuit[/b] (plus a short layout variation)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Lamborghini Huracán LMGT3 Evo2[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Lexus RC F LMGT3[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]With these additions, [i]Le Mans Ultimate[/i] now features 11 circuits with 21 layouts, 11 Hypercars, 1 LMP2, 4 GTEs, and 9 LMGT3s - 25 cars in total.[/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Refinements, Fixes & More[/b][/h3][p]We’ve made significant improvements under the hood too. These include:[/p][list][*][p]Updates to the LMGT3 tyre model for more realistic handling[/p][/*][*][p]Better race starts with class grouping and spacing[/p][/*][*][p]Smarter fuel-saving tools and MFD readouts[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]What’s Next?[/b][/h3][p]This isn’t the finish line - far from it. On June 13, we’ll be joining the ACO press conference in Le Mans and releasing another keynote video from Stephen Hood to reveal the next steps in the journey of [i]Le Mans Ultimate[/i]. We’ll be sharing a first look at what comes after this update and you won’t want to miss it.[/p][p]Until then, assemble your team, fine-tune those liveries, and get ready to race.[/p][p]We’ll see you on track.[/p]

tags.feature: From delivering driver swaps to building out full team functionality and unleashing a brand-new custom livery system, this update takes endurance racing in [i]Le Mans Ultimate[/i] to the next level.

You can now share your car with a teammate during online endurance events and hand over control mid-race just like in real-world WEC.

notes.title: Le Mans Ultimate June 2025 Update
notes.content:
Le Mans Ultimate, the official game of the FIA World Endurance Championship and 24 Hours of Le Mans is completing the 2024 Season with remaining content when the fifth and final 2024 DLC pack goes on sale on June 10th bringing 2 new LMGT3 cars and 1 new track to the game on 10th June 2025.

Along with new content, the game will receive a major update focused on mutli-driver team races, livery customisation and team management, opening the experience for longer races and showcase the endurance spirit.

[h3]Driver swaps[/h3]
We will be introducing our first events where players will hand over the car mid-race during live online endurance events using the new driver swap feature.

Teams will be able to enjoy the strategy and team-work required to share in a car’s success or failure over multi-hour races. After registering for the event as part of a team, players and their teammates are able to swap in the pitlane by using the driver field in the multi-function display (or MFD).

Compared to our previous titles, we have made various core code changes to improve security, performance and functionality. When anyone now joins a server, the game knows which car you have access to, enabling your teammates to configure your pitstops. This has the additional bonus of allowing any team member to resume from the pitlane in the unfortunate case of a technical issue.

What’s the state of this feature in the release? Well, whilst we have intensively tested this internally, with the help of some community members, the large scale performance testing of servers and driver swap information many hours into a race is not an easy task for a team of our size. Therefore we are releasing it first only in “Special Events” so we can closely monitor performance and make adjustments in our own environment.

Upcoming team-based Special Events will be published across our social media and in-game channels so keep an eye on those to find out when these will be available.

In future, we will be expanding these races to create new Team-based Online Championships and to leagues via racecontrol.gg and Sim Grid as we gain confidence in the feature’s robustness.

[h3]Team Management[/h3]
Rather than just allowing one-off entries into races, we’ve created a team dynamic for in Le Mans Ultimate, powered by RaceControl, that allows players to create a team identity and invite their friends to it. As team owner you will then be able to assign your teammates different roles and attach them to cars (or “line ups”).
You’ll find “Teams” available within the new drop down menu in the top right of the screen. From this you can see your invites, accept or reject them, or create your own team directly inside the game itself.

When creating a team, players will be able to upload a logo and also a background page for all your team mates to see and will be used elsewhere in event pages.
Here’s a bit more information about the roles that are available:

[b]Driver [/b]- What it says on the tin, drivers drive the car and that is all they do

[b]Engineer[/b] - This role will allow a player to be on the server, see data from the car and session whilst also being able to make pitstop changes. As you can see on the new watch screen that we are making available for team races, there’s quite a lot of detail to sink your teeth into. The engineer role, if used correctly, can be an invaluable contributor to your team’s success… or failure.

[b]Manager[/b] - this role allows a team member to assign players to different car line ups, assign liveries and register them for races.

[b]Team Owner[/b] - has all of the aforementioned but can also change ownership

Everyone can make a team of up to 6 members with 1 line up. For those players that want to have larger teams the team owner will need to to be a RaceControl Pro or Pro+ subscriber, enabling the ability to have up to 100 members and up to 10 line ups.

[h3]Custom Liveries[/h3]
Our brand new livery system will allow players to upload a livery to apply to a car on a particular team, and then automatically transmitted to all drivers and spectators on a server. For now, this feature is only available for online events - both single driver and team-based.

Since this feature requires significant backend infrastructure and bandwidth to automatically send the liveries across to all competitors - this feature is only available to RaceControl Pro and Pro+ players but Lite players in a team based race where the Team Owner has a Pro account will also be able to utilise custom liveries in those events.

When a livery is selected for your online event, it will automatically be transferred to all the other players on the grid so they can see your paint scheme in all it’s glory.

One warning however - players will be able to report liveries in the post-race reporting and breaking the terms of use of the service could result in serious and even permanent bans from the online service.

This is something many of you have requested since launch, and we’re thrilled to make it available in in all RaceControl events. In future, they’ll be available for private servers as well but will require pre-registration of the cars you will be driving. Whether you're building your dream design or repping your team sponsors, custom liveries let your creativity shine through.

Whilst this feature is only available for online sessions for now, in future we hope to expand this to single player Race Weekend as well.

[h3]2024 Season Completed![/h3]
Pack 5, also releasing on 10th June is the final one for the 2024 FIA WEC season. Lusail International Circuit, the opening race of the world championship is making its debut in Le Mans Ultimate. Utilising the latest laser scan from summer 2024, we’ve built this once again with Studio 397’s famed attention to detail. Floodlit and fast, Lusail offers a unique mix of technical corners and long straights — perfect for multiclass racing and offering a unique challenge.
Not only that - but we’re also adding the “short circuit” that is likely to be spicy and full of action as it cuts out the majority of the circuit’s slower sector 2.

Joining the LMGT3 class are two highly anticipated cars. Firstly, the Lamborghini Huracán LMGT3 Evo2 as run by both Iron Lynx and the Iron Dames in 2024, but sadly missing from the 2025 grid. Additionally, the fan-favourite Lexus RC F LMGT3, offers a distinct look and feel to the GT grid and will no doubt become one of the most popular cars on track.
With this final 2024 pack added, the game now offers a grand total of 11 circuits with 21 layouts, 11 hypercars, 1 LMP2, 4 GTEs and 9 LMGT3s - 25 in total.

[h3]Other Updates[/h3]
The LMGT3 tyre model has had another significant refinement, particularly aimed at reducing the potential abuse of slip angle and increasing low-speed weight, whilst keeping the stability and predictability of the tyre that players have come to expect - as always with plenty of feedback from real-world drivers - we hope it is something players will enjoy.

Race starts have had a bit of a polish, including the class splits being respected. This means that classes are now correctly grouped together, even if they don’t qualify and class pole position will also receive the best side of the grid. We’ve also implemented gaps between classes as well- meaning that by the time the LMGT3s turn up at turn 1, hopefully the Hypercars have sorted out their mess!

For fuel-saving aficionados - the clutch pedal has now been disabled above 1st gear, meaning players will have to lift and coast normally like the rest of us! Additionally, the fuel tab on the multi-function display (or MFD) has been completely revised so that you can access some interesting information about your consumption and allowing you to set lap targets to extend your stint by with warnings if your engineer doesn’t think you’ll make it.

We’ve also made some significant updates to the game by removing a middleware layer that would often crash but leave no actionable information for the development team. Whilst you won’t see any changes here, this change should enable us in future to make more progress with this type of issue.

As always, this is just a small taste of the improvements we’re bringing with this update, make sure to check out the full release notes when they are made available.

[h3]Message from the Studio[/h3]
Stephen Hood, CEO of Motorsport Games and Head of Studio 397 said "We are so excited to bring the final 2024 content to the game, as well as introduce major multiplayer and customisation features which we are confident will b popular with players. As for what's next, tune in on Friday 13th June during the 24 Hours Le Mans ACO Press Conference where we will have some exciting news to share…”

notes.title: February 2025 - Update #4 - Public release notes
notes.content:
[h3]Headlines - Game[/h3]
[list]
[*] Various improvements to AI behaviour
[*] Added toggleable Tyre Warmers
[*] Various updates to Limited Tyre Rules
[*] Championship Protests Point Reductions available for human admins
[*] Various HUD Improvements including improved Timing, Standings and Damage information
[/list]
[h3]Headlines - Content[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added Aston Martin Vantage AMR GT3 Evo as part of DLC Pack 4
[*] Added Ferrari 499p Joker Package
[*] Added Ford Mustang LMGT3 as free DLC

notes.title: Le Mans Ultimate February 2025 Update
notes.content:
[b][list]
[*] 2024 Pack 4 is here and brings more LMGT3 cars to the game on February 25th
[*] 3 new cars including the Ford Mustang LMGT3 FREE for all players
[*] Update includes revised tyre model for LMGT3 & HUD improvements  
[/list][/b]

Le Mans Ultimate, the official game of the FIA World Endurance Championship and 24 Hours of Le Mans is bolstering the LMGT3 grid with brand new cars. The fourth 2024 DLC pack goes on sale on February 25th bringing 3 new LMGT3 cars to the game, including the second FREE LMGT3 car.

Along with new content, the game will receive a new and refined HUD following players feedback, plus improvements to the AI in single player mode.  

[h3]More LMGT3 join the grid[/h3]
Proving the most popular class in Le Mans Ultimate since being introduced last year, we’re proud to add to 3 brand new cars to the LMGT3 and increasing competitiveness & variety on the grid. The latest installment to the 2024 Season Pass, 2024 Pack 4 includes 2 cars from legendary 24 Hours Le Mans brands, the Porsche 911 GT3 R LMGT3 and Aston Martin Vantage AMR LMGT3. 

In addition to Pack 4, we’re delighted to release the second FREE LMGT3 car to the platform, the Ford Mustang LMGT3! Bringing the V8 thunder, this fan favourite has been hugely requested so we are thrilled to be able to bring it to Le Mans Ultimate and available to download for FREE for all early access players. 

Popular and competitive in many race series and presenting very different driving experiences, the new additions will no doubt be welcomed and enjoyed on track by the community. 

2024 Season Pack 4 will be available to purchase at an early access price via Steam for just  [b]£5.99 / €6.99 / $7.49[/b] on the February 25th. The 2024 DLC Season Pass remains available, allowing players to access the latest content the minute it is ready to be brought into the game. Priced at just [b]£39.99 / €45.99 / $48.99[/b], the Season Pass offers a saving of around 25% compared to purchasing all packs individually. The 2024 Season Pass bundles together all five packs, which includes the four new 2024 Hypercars, four iconic circuits and seven of the closely matched LMGT3 cars.

Players who have already purchased the money-saving Season Pass will automatically receive the latest content when they update the game via Steam on the February 25th - plus the newly announced Pack 5 which is expected in early May and will included the remaining 2024 content. 
 
[h3]Enhanced LMGT3 Tyre Model[/h3]
We’re excited to receive community feedback on our improved tyre model - a significant update from the last release. Working with real world drivers and data, we’ve been able to update the model. This is arriving first for the LMGT3 class - once refined, players can expect the other classes to receive updates to their models.

What’s different? Well, the overall feeling should be both more realistic and stable, enabling players to push with confidence throughout theirstint. This was one of the biggest pieces of feedback from our “real-world” driver testers and we believe we’ve made a significant step forwards.

The balance has shifted slightly more rearwards, creating a more stable feeling and should allow more aggressive setups to enter an operating window. There’s also more load sensitivity on the rear tyres, which will reduce the the “push” found typically at higher speeds. Additionally, the slip curve along with the transient thermal grip loss have been tightened up, resulting in more grip and performance loss from pushing the tyre beyond its limits.

We’ve also tuned thermal degradation slightly upwards, reducing the benefits from aggressive sliding particularly over longer stints - taking care of your tyres is essential for endurance racing!

[h3]HUD[/h3]
And finally, a key update for this release, we’ve taken a hard look at trying to improve the data players have access to while driving.

The standings in the top left of the screen have been expanded to include tyre compound and virtual energy data - just as teams have on their competitors in real-life competition. Players will also be able to see if drivers around you have any penalties upcoming.

The Multi-Function Display (or MFD for short) has had improvements made to the sign posting of which cars are directly in competition with you. There’s now a gradient red for drivers that are or about to be a lap ahead and blue for drivers a lap behind.

In the top-right section of the screen players will find the addition of their “last lap” showcased on the screen to help awareness of current performance. Additionally, the delta has been given a “reset delta” keybind and the sector splits have been re-assessed to ensure accuracy. There’s also an estimated number of laps when in the race session which is based on the top category that should help you when inputting the amount of virtual energy required when needing a splash and dash.

One of our most highly-voted requests on the community forum - a damage display - has also been added. Players will see four states - white for normal, yellow for minor damage, red for major and flashing red for something being missing… probably worth a pitstop at that point.

[h3]Message from the Studio[/h3]
Stephen Hood, CEO of Motorsport Games and Head of Studio 397 said “As always, we are delighted to bring more content and improvements to Le Mans Ultimate” commented Stephen Hood, CEO and President of Motorsport Games. “The last update in December 2024 brought a significant increase in players to the game whilst increasing the play time and churn. We believe these improvements, new cars and additional circuit layouts will delight the game’s fans and keep them engaged with a game that continues to move in a positive direction”

notes.title: Community Update - 2025 next releases
notes.content:
[b]Hello LMU community,[/b]

We hope you all enjoyed the holiday season! It seems like the latest update (bought to you on the 10th December) kept you busy throughout (and us with server and patch maintenance)!

The team at Studio 397 have been very excited to see the positive reaction from fans, with an increase in player, social media and streaming activity since the latest major release which included the first of the long-awaited LMGT3 cars. We also kept the fixes and quality-of-life tweaks coming with large patches on the 18th December and 21st January (plus 3 hotfixes!).

As we’ve re-assessed the release schedule for 2025 with fresh eyes, we believe that some of our planned work needs a bit more time to give you the highest possible quality updates. Here’s a run-down on our next two release timelines:

[h3]Update 4 (Expected late February)[/h3]
On the content side, we will be bringing 3 new LMGT3 cars (1 will be a free Early Access DLC item). Unfortunately, Lusail International Circuit (Qatar) is not going to be ready for this release as we strive for the greatest accuracy and waited for the latest laser scan (from July 2024). Therefore 2024 Pack 4 will consist of 2 cars and a new 2024 Pack 5 will be created for the remaining 2 cars and circuit – if you’re a Season Pass holder, this will be added automatically to your account. For major features - we previously said we would be trying to bring Teams and Driver Swaps to this release but unfortunately this needs more time and will move to Update 5. We will be bringing some new layouts to existing circuits in the game, free to all owners of those tracks, to add more variety to both your online and offline experiences – stay tuned to see exactly what is coming (along with various other quality-of-life improvements) when we make a larger announcement about this update.

[h3]Update 5 (Expected early May)[/h3]
As mentioned above – this release will include Driver Swaps and Teams as headline features as well as Custom Liveries for RaceControl Pro and Pro+ members. Teams and Driver Swaps, manageable directly inside the game , will be available to all users in Hosted and Special Events, plus a new Team Online Championship mode will be added for RaceControl Pro and Pro+ subscribers.

[url=https://lemansultimate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Got-Invited-2.png][img]https://lemansultimate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Got-Invited-2.png[/img][/url]

Custom Liveries will allow users to upload their Team identity (usable in single driver events as well) directly to RaceControl and automatically download liveries as you join races – exciting stuff!

The release of the new “Pack 5” will come at this point, including the previously mentioned two LMGT3 cars and Qatar.

As always, you can expect more quality-of-life improvements when the full announcement is made for this release.

[h3]Releases after Update 5[/h3]

These are still to be determined from both a feature and content perspective, but rest assured there’s a lot more to come for Le Mans Ultimate.

We’re always happy to hear your thoughts by submitting and upvoting features here: https://community.lemansultimate.com/index.php?forums/feature-requests.5/


We appreciate delays can be frustrating but rest assured that we’ve made these decisions only because we are determined to deliver to you features and content only when they are in a suitable state and ready for the feedback that you would expect to be able to give during Early Access.

Thanks to everyone for all your support and here’s to another big year for Le Mans Ultimate in 2025!

notes.title: December 2024 - Update #3 - Public release notes
notes.content:
Build: 

[h3]Headlines Updates[/h3]
[list]
[*] Improvements to AI tyre temperature simulation resulting in a better correlation to player tyre warmup.
[*] Improved VR support
[*] Large scale memory usage optimisation resulting in higher FPS during more contested scenes
[*] Improved texture loading performance with improvements of around 30%
[*] Added new Online menu
[*] Improved event lobby screen for all online modes
[*] Added the ability to host your own lobbies via RaceControl.GG
[*] Added Online Championships feature for RaceControl Pro
[*] Daily Race future event access and practice for RaceControl Pro
[*] Added HTML Broadcast Overlay system with WEC styling
[*] Fix for AMD memory leaks (as seen in Update 2, Patch 1, Hotfix 2)
[/list]
[h3]Headlines - Content[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added McLaren 720S LMGT3 Evo as [b]FREE DLC[/b]
[*] Added Corvette Z06 LMGT3.R as part of DLC Pack 3
[*] Added BMW M4 LMGT3 as part of DLC Pack 3
[*] Added Ferrari 296 LMGT3 as part of DLC Pack 3
[*] Added Interlagos as part of DLC Pack 3
[*] [b]Tyre/Aero updates[/b] - The "edge" on both tyre and aero has been softened. Locking the brakes (especially at front) is now less easy. There is a little bit more grip at higher speeds and a less aggressive drop-off when at or slightly over the limit.
[*] [b]Tyre Physics[/b] - Adjusted temperature warm-up curve to provide less grip at low tyre temperatures. Adjusted grip drop-off with temperature & pressure sensitivity based on slip. Slightly less aggressive curve.
[/list]
[h3]Game Updates[/h3]
[b]Achievements[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed "A Day At The Races" achievement not tracking when completing laps in the Porsche 911.
[/list]
[b]AI[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed AI tyre logic which would lead to AI always pitting the first lap after coming out of the pits in damp conditions.
[*] Reworked AI lapping logic on straights so they no longer aim for gaps that don't exist, hoping the other car gets out of the way
[*] Fix for physics thread slow downs when lots of AI are on a straight
[*] Improved AI settings so you can now set Aggression Low - Medium - High. This scales according to difficulty and Limiter is set automatically with this too
[/list].
[b]Cockpit Displays[/b]
[list]
[*] Removed translation on N and R gears so that they show on non-English languages
[/list].
[b]Co-op[/b]
[list]
[*] Update to allow restricted classes by event
[*] Added support for limited vehicle availability
[/list]
[b]Driver Labels[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed crash from driver labels when exiting game
[/list]
[b]Graphics[/b]
[list]
[*] Adjusted lighting balance as ambient was often too blue.
[*] Updated cameras to stay onboard cars when returning to garage
[/list]
[b]HUD[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed engineer message "One Lap To Go" being displayed more than once.
[*] Added ABS adjustability to MFD electronics page
[*] Fixed "One Lap to Go" message often being shown wrong, and added follow up messages when the situation changes.
[*] Improved weather information on session MFD page
[*] Fixed degrees character not rendering properly when changing FOV in game
[/list]
[b]Input[/b]
[list]
[*] Fix for keyboard key combinations not working correctly from some users such as adjusting seat, mirrors or pitch.
[*] Removed Steering Torque Capability setting, as this would often result in incorrect FFB configuration.
[*] Added control mapping for ABS increase/decrease
[/list]
[b]Limited Tyre Rules[/b]
[list]
[*] Added Limited Tyres online support
[/list]
[b]Localisation[/b]
[list]
[*] Corrected some errors with localisation text
[/list]
[b]Physics[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed Virtual Energy lap count calculation being incorrect when returning to the garage after starting their first lap without completing it at Sebring.
[*] Improvements to Tyre Physics to allow increase in slip related dropoff with cold tyres.
[*] Fixes for real road drying line calculations not working
[*] Reviewed Real Road clearing of rubber in the rain
[/list]
[b]Online[/b]
[list]
[*] Added future Daily Race cards
[*] Fixed join event button not refreshing after event has started
[*] Fix for post-race online results screen not showing
[*] Fix for viewing past event results always showing todays date.
[*] Updated the event countdown bar to count down not up
[*] Improved handling of split & event cancelled notifications
[*] Fixed finish position not showing up on recent event cards
[*] Fixed "Page Not Found" error when clicking during "event changeover" trying to access online event pages
[*] Fix for 0 appearing on the standings screen in online racing monitor next to the session time.
[/list]
[b]Race Starts[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed formation line issues on full formation lap when Safety car pits
[*] Fixed fast rolling start at Le Mans causing player disqualification when following starting instructions in LMP2 or GT car
[*] Fixed inconsistencies in the race start guide causing drivers to receive penalties
[*] Fixed a situation in which the formation user experience may break if the leader does not grid
[/list]
[b]Replay[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed stuttering/judder when viewing replay with the replay UI displayed
[*] Fixed a game crash when loading an old replay
[/list]
[b]Save & Load[/b]
[list]
[*] Improved robustness of Save Game format
[*] Fixed car MFD value adjustment not being stored in game saves
[*] Fix for full damage repair always taking 180s after loading a save game
[*] Fix for saved damage not being restored when restarting stints.
[*] Fixed some of the car setup settings return to default when loading a saved game.
[/list]
[b]Settings & Profiles[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed some issues around setting screen resolution when monitors have changed
[*] Disabled ABS driving aid in in game settings menu when current car is equipped with in car ABS (LMGT3)
[*] Added ABS map to car setup menu
[*] Update FOV key bind control so that default sits correctly in the sequence
[*] Added anti-roll bar bindings to car controls
[*] Updated graphics settings page to force confirmation of unapplied changes when leaving screen.
[/list]
[b]Sound[/b]
[list]
[*] Fix various issues surrounding headphones including initialisation, lack of bass response, and HRTF selection
[*] Improved code support for ABS and TC sound
[/list]
[b]User Interface[/b]
[list]
[*] Full Screen - when the game is in full screen window mode the game will always be the active window even though other windows are in focus on top of it
[*] Fix for booting the game in full screen mode on an AMD will often crash or take a long time to boot
[*] Updated and improved car renders for in game car select screens
[*] Updated Main Menu Order
[*] Removed corner UI animations to improve CEF rendering
[*] Updated tyre compound UI colours match official WEC scheme
[*] Updated damage simulation settings in advanced options to show fixed options rather than a percentage slider
[*] Fixed online race notification overlapping page titles at the top left of the screen
[/list]
[b]Virtual Reality[/b]
[list]
[*] Added VR mirror option to graphics settings page
[*] Added VR related key binds to UI
[*] Added configurable VR UI and HUD render size
[*] Fix for undercar shadows only rendering in one eye
[*] Adjusted Spectator Camera clip planes to prevent clipping when looking around
[*] Added VR specific HUD
[*] Revised PFX settings for VR and revised glare settings in general
[*] Desaturate environment when in menus in VR.
[*] Temporarily disabled motion blur in VR, due to it only working in one eye
[*] Updated VR defaults settings on first launch to 1920x1080 VR Mirror and low PFX
[*] Fixed applying any Display changes whilst in VR causing the game to freeze
[*] Improved UX around out of focus game window in VR by desaturating screen when game isn't in focus
[/list]
[b]Voice Over[/b]
[list]
[*] Added missing Green Flag Voice Over at Le Mans
[/list]
[b]Track Updates[/b]
[b]General[/b]
[list]
[*] Updated all tracks Real Road presets for better and more consistent grip distribution.
[/list]
[b]Circuit of the Americas  [/b]
[list]
[*] Removed collisions from fuelling rigs
[*] Updated back straight track limits to not allow red side aprons
[/list]
[list]
[b]Portimao[/b] 
[list]
[*] Removed collisions from fuelling rigs
[*] Fixed AI braking when switching to pit path.
[*] Fixed white line pit exit track limits detection not working
[/list]
[b]Circuit de la Sarthe[/b]  
[list]
[*] Corrected which side of the track Pole Position takes the green flag from
[/list]
[b]Imola[/b]  
[list]
[*] Corrected which side of the track Pole Position takes the green flag from
[*] Fixed pit stands smoothing issues
[/list]
[b]Sebring[/b]  
[list]
[*] Corrected which side of the track Pole Position takes the green flag from
[/list]
[b]Bahrain 2023[/b]  
[list]

notes.title: Le Mans Ultimate December 2024 update
notes.content:
[h3]Le Mans Ultimate welcomes LMGT3, Hosted Servers and New Online Subscriptions services.[/h3]
[list]
[*] 2024 Pack 3 is here and brings LMGT3 class to the game on December 10th
[*] 4 new cars with the McLaren 720S LMGT3 Evo FREE for all players 
[*] Interlagos track arrives as part of the 2024 WEC season content
[*] Online Championships, Hosted Servers and Optional Subscription tiers launching
[/list] 
Le Mans Ultimate, the official game of the FIA World Endurance Championship and 24 Hours of Le Mans is welcoming a new category, LMGT3. The third 2024 DLC pack goes on sale on December 10th delivering 4 new LMGT3 cars to the game as well as the iconic Brazilian Interlagos circuit. All players will also be able to download the first of 2 LMGT3 cars. 

The December update marks the launch of the frequently requested Hosted Server feature, built upon our RaceControl Online service. Players can now configure and run their own Practice, Qualifying and Race events. Furthermore, Online Championships arrive in LMU as part of an expanding service supported by differing subscription tiers. A custom Broadcast Overlay, as well as a variety of quality of life updates, complement our biggest service update thus far.

[b]Revealing the LMGT3 contenders[/b]
LMGT3 is the latest category to join the World Endurance Championship, and is arguably  the most competitive and closely fort classes. With recognisable and relatable cars, easy to drive/hard to master handling and a long list to choose from, the category is favoured by real world and sim racers alike. Our latest 2024 Season Pack 3 DLC is the introduction to the class, bringing the BMW M4 LMGT3, Corvette Z06 LMGT3.R and Ferrari 296 LMGT3, plus the McLaren 720S LMGT3 Evo available to download for free to all early access players of Le Mans Ultimate.

Each car, painstakingly modelled by Studio 397, brings their own unique configuration and driving characteristics. This new class of cars will prove to be an exciting, absorbing challenging that will appeal to new and existing players alike. 

[b]But it is not just cars included in 2024 Season Pack 3…. [/b]
A fan favourite and making a return in 2024 after a 10 year hiatus from the World Endurance Championship, Autódromo José Carlos Pace (or commonly known as Interlagos) joins the Le Mans Ultimate roster of fast and flowing drivers tracks. Laser scanned and featuring the level of detail accustom to S397 tracks, the iconic green, yellow and white kerbs are a rare & special sight in sim racing and we’re delighted to recognise this experience in Le Mans Ultimate. 

2024 Season Pack 3 will be available to purchase at an early access price via Steam for just £13.99 / €16.99 / $17.99 on the December 10th. The 2024 DLC Season Pass remains available, allowing players to access the latest content the minute it is ready to be brought into the game. Priced at just £39.99 / €45.99 / $48.99, the Season Pass offers a saving of around 25% compared to purchasing all four packs individually. The 2024 Season Pass bundles together all four packs, which includes the four new 2024 Hypercars, four iconic circuits and seven of the closely matched GT3 cars.

Players who have already purchased the money-saving Season Pass will automatically receive the latest content when they update the game via Steam on the 10th December. 

[b]But December is not just about content…[/b] 

[b]Hosted[/b]
Ranked amongst the top requested features since launch, you will now be able to race in organised leagues or just with your friends with the launch of hosted servers. Working with our partners SimGrid to power RaceControl.gg, players will be able to purchase server credits to run their very own race or league with scalable pricing depending on server size from as little as €0.38 per hour (note: local taxes may apply). Servers can be configured via the website, and either displayed in the public lobby list with or without password, or found simply by a 5 character code that will both find the server and enter the password for a user. 

[b]Overlay[/b]
Together with the ability to host your own server, we are also releasing a spectate mode to the game which allows players to join a server without being a driver and created a broadcast overlay in the FIA World Endurance Championship style so you and your league can broadcast to your preferred streaming platform. The broadcast overlay outputs to HTML outside of the game and can be used as a transparent layer in most streaming tools, such as OBS. As an advanced user feature, there will be a user guide on how to configure it.

[b]Online Championships & Subscriptions[/b] 
RaceControl Pro is a brand new service designed to elevate the entertainment value for invested Le Mans Ultimate players. Bringing enhanced online competitions, including the frequently requested Online Championship format which enables players to battle through multiple rounds of an ongoing and epic story through multiple seasons. This service provides the ability to register and practice for daily races not in rotation plus enhanced player reporting designed to assist in making racing in our RaceControl led events respectful.

RaceControl Pro is an optional subscription tier which, if purchased through an upfront annual plan, works out at an incredible price €3.50* viewed monthly. A further premium tier, RaceControl Pro+, available for a monthly equivalent of €6.50*, provides players with all of the RaceControl Pro benefits but unlocks all Studio 397 DLC content - yes, for rFactor 2 as well - for as long as their subscription is active. For players looking to gain access to whatever they want when they want, RaceControl Pro+ removes the barriers to the full suite of features and content across all RaceControl connected games, which today means the legendary sandbox simulator rFactor 2 and the more recent still in rapid development Le Mans Ultimate. All previous event types including Daily, Weekly and Special races will remain accessible to all players regardless of subscription level.

Online Championships has been designed for players that want more from their online experience, battling for supremacy in the Le Mans Ultimate ranking tables and having a structure & consistency to their racing schedule. These races are less frequent than daily races, on particular days of the week, across different timezones and with a limited number of attempts per week depending upon the difficulty of the championship. As per other championship modes, players register for the championship and will be required to commit to a particular car throughout the season. We will be using these championships in future to run competitions, including esports series like Le Mans Virtual Series and for our partners.

There are more benefits coming in future - watch this space. To sign up, visit racecontrol.gg or follow one of the in-game links.

*Annual subscription, local taxes may apply

[b]Message from the Studio[/b]
Stephen Hood, CEO of Motorsport Games and Head of Studio 397 said “We are incredibly excited to present to players the hotly anticipated LMGT3 category into the game along with a suite of enhancements and feature updates. The additional private server hosting will enable the passionate and growing community to create their own events and live out their endurance racing dreams. We can’t wait to see how players leverage the growing suite of tools made available through RaceControl to build bespoke experiences and communities around a shared love of Le Mans Ultimate.”

“The optional RaceControl Pro subscription includes a unique Online Championship mode that ramps up the importance and excitement of races powered by skill-based matchmaking and will in future host the future  qualifying for our important Le Mans Virtual Series esports series.” continued Hood. “The premium Pro+ tier of RaceControl is a landmark moment in our ambition to integrate games, features and content within a seamless platform for the benefit of our players who now have incredible choice in how they consume the entertainment we provide.”

“We sincerely hope players enjoy this update as the passionate Studio 397 team continue to pour their hardwork into making this FIA WEC experience the best it can be, with many more exciting updates planned for 2025.”

notes.title: Le Mans Ultimate September 2024 Update
notes.content:
Le Mans Ultimate, the official game of the FIA World Endurance Championship and 24 Hours of Le Mans is preparing to do battle stateside in the second Downloadable Content (DLC) pack, which goes on sale Tuesday 24th September. The Texan shootout at the Circuit of Americas hosts the French flair of Alpine and the adventures of Isotta Fraschini as well as a whole host of free content, quality of life updates and new gameplay feature, Co-op mode in the latest drop.

[b]Peeking inside Pack 2[/b]
The spirit of Le Mans heads to the USA, with the arrival of the Circuit of the Americas to Le Mans Ultimate. COTA returned to the FIA World Endurance Championship calendar in 2024 and creates its own unique set of challenges to sports car racing teams. From the dry desert heat to its challenging nature and flow of the circuit –the Texan lap offers fast and flowing turns in sector one and tight and twisty sections in the second half of the lap.

The Alpine A424, from the French sports car manufacturer –conjures up the magic and mystique of sports car racing from yesteryear. It’s angular, purposeful looks, complete with vibrant Mecachrome 3.4-litre V6 engine note makes the A424 stand out on the FIA WEC grid. A new car to the 2024 season, the pace and momentum of Alpine has been building with every round. Can you get them over the line and claim that first win for ‘le bleu’?

The Tipo 6 Competizione from boutique Italian manufacturer Isotta Fraschini completes the 2024 FIA WEC Hypercar grid in Le Mans Ultimate. The car and team have all the ingredients for success, and players will be able to continue the legacy for the indie marque, taking the fight to the establishment behind the wheel of the Tipo 6 Competizione. How high up the points can you climb?

The red, white and blue inspired pack two will be available to purchase at an early access price via Steam for just £9.99 / €11.99 /$12.99 on the 24th September. The 2024 DLC Season Pass is also available, allowing players to access the latest content the minute it is ready to be brought into the game. Priced at just £39.99 / €46.99 / $48.99, the pass offers a saving of almost 25% compared to purchasing all four packs individually. The 2024 Season Pass bundles together all four packs, which includes the four new 2024 Hypercars, four iconic circuits and seven of the closely matched GT3 cars which will come in the two final larger packs.

Players who have already purchased the money saving Season Pass will automatically receive the latest content when they update the game via Steam on the 24th September.

[b]There is even more content on the way…[/b]
Further to the optional DLC pack and Season Pass, all Early Access players will be able to experience fresh content, updates and a new game mode as part of the September update.

Players will be able to update the game on Steam on the 24th September, and by doing so, Le Mans Ultimate fans will receive a whole host of liveries to take to the track, as well as updates to try. Several Hypercar liveries from Le Mans including the two one off entry Cadillacs, the historic themed Proton Competition Porsche 963 as well as the JOTA Porsche, Mobil1 Celebration livery from COTA. All of these and all the Le Mans specific number board options for each Hypercar will be in your virtual garage at the end of the month.

The hugely competitive LMP2 class featured at the 24-hour classic in June this year and the popular category is a favourite in Le Mans Ultimate. All players will now be able to drive a further 16, new official 2024 liveries in offline or online race modes next week.

Following feedback from the Community Survey, some features have been brought forward, to be included in the latest game update. These include Save and Resume as well as Season Select. A feature high on the wishlist – Save and Resume will allow the player to complete longer races by saving the progress during a single player Race Weekend endurance race and resume the progress at a later date.

Season select will enable the player to compete against cars from the current FIA WEC season or go back in time to relive the golden centenary season from 2023.

[b]Pass the race to friends – Co-op mode arrives in Le Mans Ultimate[/b]
An early version of Co-op mode becomes the latest gameplay feature in Le Mans Ultimate – allowing players to play with friends, take on race challenges and compete against other teams on a global leaderboard via an asynchronous gameplay mode. Players can form a team with friends and take on some of the biggest tests in sports car racing. Racing against the AI on track – as a collective team, you will earn points based on position, overtakes and clean conduct which gets tallied up as the race duration unfolds. The final score collected as a team will place you on a leaderboard, ranking you against other teams around the world.

And the best part… you can race your way, in your own time, before passing the race onto your teammate. Immersing yourself deep into strategic decisions at the pitstop, discuss with your teammates the big calls before handing the baton onto the next driver – building a strong dynamic for a successful sportscar racing team. Complete your stint at a time that suits you and your teammates, as you not only work around the challenges on track as well as the everyday life of family and work commitments or time zone constraints.

[b]Message from the Studio[/b]
“The last few months have been really productive for Studio 397,” explained Studio 397 CEO Stephen Hood. “We have made great strides in content development and we are delighted to offer plenty for the community to get their teeth into this month. The second DLC pack introducers another new circuit to the game, with the challenging COTA – a new circuit for many to learn. We are also delighted to complete the Hypercar field with two very unique and interesting cars from Alpine and Isotta Fraschini. Two cars with their own, strong and supportive fanbases – which will hopefully provide plenty of competitive battles online.

“As well as the DLC we have plenty of free content for all Early Access supporters. As well as a few new Hypercar liveries we have an entire grid of LMP2 cars ready to be enjoyed. We know that class is loved by many of the Le Mans Ultimate community. Those looking for a more enjoyable playing experience will also be able to save progress and resume at a later date in single payer mode, as well as a fresh UI and navigation in the menus to provide a more cohesive user journey.

“Co-op is something many have been patiently waiting for, and we are delighted to bring the first version to the game. Life can be pretty hectic, so we have created a fun and dynamic game mode allowing you to race with friends and take on challenges in your own time – when it is convenient to you. Playing with friends is a big priority for us in developing the need for teamwork in sportscar racing, and this is a big first step to open up other opportunities for future game modes, challenges and even qualification into esports events.

“For those eagle-eyed, you will have noticed the Hypercar grid is now complete. This means we have started work on LMGT3 content – which I know so many of you have been craving. We hope to have the third 2024 DLC pack and more gameplay features ready by the end of the year, as well as the next free car to go alongside it all.”

Sim racers will be able to wishlist the second pack on Steam ahead of going on sale later this month. Those not yet on the grid can take advantage of the base game introductory price of £24.99/ €29.99 / $32.99 until the 30th September, when the price will then be set at £29.99/€34.99 / $37.99 to reflect the increase in content and game play features. The base game features all of the Hypercars and circuits from the 2023 Centenary season as well as the classic LMP2 and GTE cars. Those already clocking the hours can also download the 2024 BMW M Hybrid V8 Hypercar for free via Steam today.

Added [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2973290/Le_Mans_Ultimate__2024_Pack_1/?snr=1_16_16_creator_1059&curator_clanid=44213141]2024 Pack 1[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2997280/Le_Mans_Ultimate__2024_Season_Pass/?snr=1_16_16_creator_1059&curator_clanid=44213141]2024 Season Pass[/url] DLC alongside a number of fixes and tweaks.

[h2]General, Code and UI/UX[/h2]
[h3]UI[/h3]
[list]
[*] Improved UI rendering performance 
[*] Changed the video driver setting label to “Monitor“
[*] Available resolutions now update based on the selected monitor
[*] Private qualify now displays correctly in race weekend event creation
[*] Removed Coach Dave from the possible save locations for car setups
[*] Stopped the first time account creation from being skipped causing a player to have no account
[*] Added new background images to the main menu
[*] Improved car select to not show loading animations twice
[*] All the unavailable symbols are showcased in account name creation
[/list]

[h3]Replay[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added the ability to access the full replay while on track via the pause menu
[*] Added the ability to skip to a specific lap in a replay
[*] Added more information to the driver panel in the bottom right
[*] Added class, manufacturer and team number
[*] Updated icons in the camera select
[*] Show the camera group selected when changing camera groups
[*] Fixed a replay-related crash when leaving online races.
[*] Replays work with the HUD correctly
[*] Fixed replay un-pause in the replay pause menu
[*] Fixed large replays crashing the game
[*] Fixed replay flickering
[/list]

[h3]Driver labels
[/h3][list]
[*] Added country flags to driver labels online and single player
[*] Fixed a scaling issue happening on some larger resolutions
[*] Added manufacturer logos to the driver labels
[*] Fixed centre-alignment of driver labels for certain cars.
[*] Fixed black artefacts on the edge of driver labels.
[*] Fixed a driver labels-related crash when exiting a session and loading a replay immediately after
[*] Fixed a driver label-related crash when moving to the next session
[/list]

[h3]Online[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed timezone selection to show the correct timezones accounting for daylight saving
[*] Fixed that some longer event names would push elements off the screen
[*] During fixed setup Multiplayer events, vehicle changes are now saved on session change
[*] Fixed a connection lost issue when qualifying ends in a Multiplayer race
[*] Fixed an issue where the rear view camera would change when a player joins a race in multiplayer.
[/list]

[h3]HUD[/h3]
[list]
[*] The pit indicator will now show on HUD elements when a car is anywhere in the pit lane and not just the pit box.
[*] Multi-stint specific HUD information now only shows in race sessions.
[*] Onboard menus like the HUD MFD can now be cycled by holding controls.
[*] Fixed the track map visibility not respecting the player settings
[*] Fixed the full-view track map being cut off on certain tracks (namely Le Mans).
[*] Various optimisations to the driver labels and driver overlay HUD elements
[/list]

[h3]Controllers
[/h3]
[list]
[*] Disconnecting a gamepad now shows the pause menu, pausing in single player.
[*] 
[/list]
[h3]AI and Driving
[/h3][list]
[*] Added Lamborghini and Porsche 99 car to “Fill Grid” option
[*] Remapped AI difficulty from 75 to 105% and added categories to indicate the difficulty of each setting
[*] Limited Tyre and Fuel wear to a maximum rate of x3 due to the impact of higher fuel values at Le Mans and the extremeness of flat spots
[*] Fixed an issue where AI cars on track would fail to react to cars leaving the pitlane
[*] Added the ability for two cars to share the same physical garage whilst having unique pit spots.
[/list]

[h3]Race Starts
[/h3][list]
[*] Fixed slow AI in chicanes during formation laps at low difficulty
[*] Improved formation lap guidance to avoid pileups caused by concertina issues
[*] Various small fixes to formation lap warnings and penalties
[*] Fixed formation lap occasionally counting drivers as 10km ahead of the leader, leading to disqualification
[*] Improved formation lap behaviour when held up by other cars, with better UX and improved scoring
[*] Fixed a condition where getting a penalty during the formation lap, then crossing the finish line before the lights go green, would result in an extra lap being added to the lap counter
[*] Improved erratic driving warning to restrict weaving and rapid acceleration/deceleration during formation laps in double file
[*] Fixed an issue where it would take around 2 minutes at Le Mans for pit exit light to go green if a driver taking the start fails to pass the pit exit. It should now take around 30 seconds
[/list]

[h3]Visuals[/h3]
[list]
[*] Improved the visual progression from dry to damp track
[*] Fixed Safety Car lodding out very quickly when it is in the pitlane
[*] Improved cockpit displays with expanded options for aligning text
[/list]

[/h3][list]
[*] Fixed a tyre temperature information-related crash
[*] Fixed the leading ":" character on chat messages
[*] Fix damage appearing on the wrong end of the car in car vs car collisions
[*] Fix electric motor (MGU) and shift sounds not playing back in replay and online
[*] Fix disallowed xml characters being able to end up in the results.xml meaning results not being able to be processed online
[*] Fixed an issue where the game would crash if there was no race leader
[*] Fix for temp car freezing in online sessions
[*] 
[/list]

notes.title: Step into the Paddock: 2024 Season Pass and first DLC pack announced
notes.content:
Le Mans Ultimate, the official game of the FIA World Endurance Championship and 24
Hours of Le Mans is excited to reveal the first Downloadable Content (DLC) Pack goes
on sale on Tuesday 23rd July. Included in the first drop will be the drivers favourite
Autodromo Internazionale Enzo e Dino Ferrari (Imola Circuit) as well as the Lamborghini
SC63 and 2024 Peugeot 9X8 which made its competitive debut at the Emilia-Romagna
circuit creating an Italian flavoured pack fit for the Tifosi. The first pack will form one
quarter of the 2024 DLC Season Pass, which will also offer further exciting content over
the coming months – with a notable overall saving.

The 2024 FIA WEC season and recent 24 Hours of Le Mans have gripped the motorsport
world, with four different teams taking victory on the opening four rounds – including
back-to-back victories for Ferrari at the fabled 24 Hours of Le Mans. As the season
enters the second half, Le Mans Ultimate is excited to showcase the new 2024 content
from the thrilling season, as asked for by the community, with the first pack and
complete Season Pass on sale later this month.

[h3]2024 Pack 1 – Tifosi Italia – The first DLC pack from Le Mans Ultimate[/h3]
The European summer hots up with two Hypercars ready to do battle at the Autodromo
Internazionale Enzo e Dino Ferrari (Imola Circuit). Imola received an enormous crowd
back in April, with over 70,000 fans across the three days when the FIA WEC visited in
the Spring. Such was its popularity, the undulating circuit nestled in northern Italy will
become a permanent feature on future calendars for the next four years – making it a
sportscar racing fixture for fans for years to come.

The striking and beautiful Lamborghini SC63 from the stable of the raging bull is a car
built with the Italian flair and passion – taking on some of the biggest manufacturers in
the world including Toyota, Porsche and Ferrari. It’s 3.8-litre V8 packs a punch, and its
exhaust note is one to stir the emotion of any motorsport fan.

Facing the Lamborghini is the might from Peugeot. Imola was chosen by the French
manufacturer to debut the all-new, 2024 evolution of its 9X8 Hypercar, with its
aggressive and purposeful looks, the fearless lion ran strongly against its regular sparing
partners on its debut back in April.

The Italian inspired pack will be available to purchase at an early access price via Steam
for just £9.99 / €11.99 / $12.99 on the 23rd July as well as the content filled 2024
Season Pass.

[h3]Access all Areas – The 2024 Season Pass[/h3]
The 2024 DLC Season Pass will be your access all areas to the current season and will
enable you to download the latest content the minute it is ready to be brought into the
game. Priced at just £39.99 / €46.99 / $49.99, the pass will offer a saving of almost
25% compared to purchasing all four packs individually. The 2024 Season Pass will
bundle together all four packs, which will include four new Hypercars, four iconic circuits
and seven of the closely matched GT3 cars in larger packs towards the end of the
schedule.

[h3]Free content is also on the way[/h3]
Following the arrival of the free BMW M Hybrid V8 Hypercar last month, all Early Access
players will be able to download two GT3 cars for free later in the season pass schedule
so everyone can experience the latest category in the championship, as well as receiving
the 2024 Le Mans Hypercar and LMP2 liveries, with further free special edition liveries
coming later this year.

Regardless of whether or not you purchase any 2024 packs, you’ll be able to race
against the 2024 grid in Le Mans Ultimate. Further information and content on the
remaining three individual packs will be teased and revealed ahead of each release, with
the next drop expected late September 2024.

[h3]Message from the Studio[/h3]
“The 2024 FIA WEC season is a must watch for any motorsport fan and I like millions of
others, was glued to the 24 Hours of Le Mans last month,” enthused Stephen Hood,
CEO of Studio 397. “The new 2024 content has been high up on the wish list of the
community, with sim racers itching to get their hands on the latest cars, liveries and
circuits to recreate those thrilling WEC moments. We were delighted with our last
update and appreciate all of the feedback from the June update, including the free BMW
Hypercar – which is proving to be a popular car online and offline.

“We are adding the Lamborghini SC63 and 2024 Peugeot 9X8 into the fray as well as
Imola, as part of our first DLC pack. All the ingredients to create some exciting online
races. 

“Development is well underway on the rest of the 2024 Season Pass Content as well as
new gameplay features and quality of life updates which we hope to bring to the market
in late September – just as the 2024 FIA WEC season reaches its exciting crescendo.”

Sim racers will be able to wishlist the 2024 Season Pass and first pack on Steam ahead
of going on sale later this month. Those not yet on the grid can take advantage of the
introductory Early Access game price of £24.99 / €29.99 / $32.99. The game features all
of the Hypercars and circuits from the 2023 Centenary season as well as the classic
LMP2 and GTE cars. Those already clocking the hours can also download the 2024 BMW
M HybridV8 Hypercar for free via Steam today.

For further news, teases and updates, be sure to follow the Le Mans Ultimate social
media accounts as well as www.lemansultimate.com which will also offer further exciting
content over the coming months with a notable overall saving
